mls-u2-q11.statement: A naive finite-difference attack targets an input with \(d=500\) features for 20 gradient steps.
mls-u2-q11.prompt: How many queries does it need?
mls-u2-q11.hint: Two queries for each feature, for each step.
solutionSteps: \(2 \times 500 = 1000\) queries per step.

mls-u2-q12.title: Label-only attacks
mls-u2-q12.statement: A team removes all confidence scores from its API and concludes that black-box evasion is now impossible. What is the best response?

options.a: Attacks can still search using final labels, though they need more queries
options.b: The attack is impossible only if the labels are also encrypted in transit
options.c: Removing the scores makes the model’s weights easy to reconstruct directly

mls-u2-q12.hint: What information does the API still return for each query?
mls-u2-q12.explanation: Decision-based attacks need only the predicted label. Removing scores increases query cost without ruling out the attack.
solutionSteps: Decision-based attacks need only the predicted label. Removing scores increases query cost without ruling out the attack.
Choose A: Attacks can still search using final labels, though they need more queries

mls-u2-q13.title: Adversarial training
mls-u2-q13.statement: A model adversarially trained under an \(L_\infty\) budget is later attacked with a large patch on a small area. What is the most reasonable expectation?

options.a: The robustness may not carry over, since this is a different threat model
options.b: The robustness carries over fully, because the same pixels are involved
options.c: The model will reject the patch, since training adds an input detector

mls-u2-q13.hint: What perturbations did the training actually include?
mls-u2-q13.explanation: Training covers the perturbations it saw. A localised patch is not bounded the same way, so robustness to it is not implied.
solutionSteps: Training covers the perturbations it saw. A localised patch is not bounded the same way, so robustness to it is not implied.
Choose A: The robustness may not carry over, since this is a different threat model

mls-u2-q14.title: Gradient masking
mls-u2-q14.statement: A defence shows higher success for a black-box attack than for a white-box attack with full access. What does this most strongly suggest?

options.a: The model is certifiably robust against every possible white-box attack
options.b: The black-box attack must have been given the model’s private weights
options.c: The gradients are being obscured and the white-box attack is failing

mls-u2-q14.hint: Full knowledge should never make an attacker worse.
mls-u2-q14.explanation: A white-box attacker can in principle do anything a black-box attacker can, so a worse result indicates that the attack is being misled by gradient masking.
solutionSteps: A white-box attacker can in principle do anything a black-box attacker can, so a worse result indicates that the attack is being misled by gradient masking.
Choose C: The gradients are being obscured and the white-box attack is failing

mls-u2-q15.title: Adaptive evaluation
mls-u2-q15.statement: Which evaluation gives the most credible evidence for a new evasion defence?

options.a: An attack built for this defence and aware of all of its components
options.b: A standard attack from a library, run with its default parameters
options.c: The same attack used on the undefended model, run for fewer steps

mls-u2-q15.hint: Which attacker has actually tried to get around the defence?
mls-u2-q15.explanation: Only an adaptive attack tests the defence against an opponent who knows it exists and targets it directly.
solutionSteps: Only an adaptive attack tests the defence against an opponent who knows it exists and targets it directly.
Choose A: An attack built for this defence and aware of all of its components

mls-u2-q16.title: Certified robustness
mls-u2-q16.statement: A Gaussian-smoothed classifier uses \(\sigma=0.25\). A statistically valid lower bound \(\underline p_A>1/2\) satisfies \(\Phi^{-1}(\underline p_A)=2\).
mls-u2-q16.hint: Multiply the noise level by the given inverse-CDF value.
mls-u2-q16.explanation: The conservative certified radius is \(R=0.25\times2=0.5\). At the bound’s confidence level, the smoothed prediction is unchanged for \(\|\delta\|_2<0.5\).
solutionSteps: Use the lower probability bound, not an empirical vote fraction.
\(R=\sigma\Phi^{-1}(\underline p_A)=0.25\times2=0.5\).
The guarantee concerns the smoothed classifier within this open L2 ball, not correctness or the base classifier.

mls-u3-q01.title: Kinds of poisoning
mls-u3-q01.statement: After retraining, overall accuracy is unchanged, but transactions from one specific merchant are now always approved. Which kind of poisoning fits best?

options.a: Availability poisoning
options.b: Targeted poisoning
options.c: Membership inference

mls-u3-q01.hint: Did the harm affect the model broadly or just a selected case?
mls-u3-q01.explanation: Accuracy elsewhere is intact and one chosen case changed, which is the targeted pattern.
solutionSteps: Accuracy elsewhere is intact and one chosen case changed, which is the targeted pattern.
Choose B: Targeted poisoning

mls-u3-q02.title: Clean-label poisoning
mls-u3-q02.statement: Why does manually checking that each label is correct fail to stop clean-label poisoning?

options.a: The poisoned records are encrypted while they are in the dataset
options.b: The poisoned records are removed again before evaluation begins
options.c: The poisoned records have correct labels and look legitimate

mls-u3-q02.hint: What specifically is the attacker not changing?
mls-u3-q02.explanation: The attack relies on the feature representation, and the labels are accurate, so a label audit finds nothing wrong.
solutionSteps: The attack relies on the feature representation, and the labels are accurate, so a label audit finds nothing wrong.

mls-u3-q03.title: Poisoning at web scale
mls-u3-q03.statement: Which control most directly prevents an attacker from swapping content behind a URL in a dataset index?

options.a: Increasing the number of training epochs used on the downloaded data
options.b: Normalising every downloaded image to the same mean and variance
options.c: Storing a cryptographic hash of each item and verifying it on download

mls-u3-q03.hint: How would you detect that the bytes differ from the original?
mls-u3-q03.explanation: A hash recorded at index time reveals any later substitution, so tampered downloads can be discarded.
solutionSteps: A hash recorded at index time reveals any later substitution, so tampered downloads can be discarded.
Choose C: Storing a cryptographic hash of each item and verifying it on download

mls-u3-q04.title: How little data is needed
mls-u3-q04.statement: An attacker contributes 500 records to a dataset that has 50,000 records in total.
mls-u3-q04.prompt: What is the poison rate, in percent?
mls-u3-q04.hint: Divide, then convert to a percentage.

mls-u3-q05.title: How backdoors work
mls-u3-q05.statement: A downloaded model scores 98% on your held-out test set. What does this tell you about backdoors?

options.a: Little, because triggers are absent from ordinary test data
options.b: It has none, because backdoored models have poor accuracy
options.c: It has none, because any trigger would be in the held-out set

mls-u3-q05.hint: Would your test set contain the attacker’s secret pattern?
mls-u3-q05.explanation: Backdoors are designed to keep clean accuracy high, so a good score on data without the trigger gives almost no evidence.
solutionSteps: Backdoors are designed to keep clean accuracy high, so a good score on data without the trigger gives almost no evidence.
Choose A: Little, because triggers are absent from ordinary test data

mls-u3-q06.title: Measuring a backdoor
mls-u3-q06.statement: A backdoor is tested on images that do not belong to the target class. Why are images that are already in the target class excluded?

options.a: They have no effect on any metric that is reported about the backdoor
options.b: They would count as successes even if there were no backdoor at all
options.c: They cannot be given a trigger because their labels are already fixed

mls-u3-q06.hint: What would the model output for those images anyway?
mls-u3-q06.explanation: A model correctly labelling a target-class image looks like a success, which would inflate the measured attack success.
solutionSteps: A model correctly labelling a target-class image looks like a success, which would inflate the measured attack success.
Choose B: They would count as successes even if there were no backdoor at all

mls-u3-q07.title: Outsourced training
mls-u3-q07.statement: A team fine-tunes only the classification head of a third-party model. Why might a backdoor survive?

options.a: The earlier layers that detect the trigger have not been changed
options.b: Fine-tuning always strengthens every backdoor present in a model
options.c: Classification heads are unable to take any input from earlier layers

mls-u3-q07.explanation: A trigger detector in frozen layers keeps producing the same features, and the new head can still learn from them.
solutionSteps: A trigger detector in frozen layers keeps producing the same features, and the new head can still learn from them.
Choose A: The earlier layers that detect the trigger have not been changed

mls-u3-q08.title: Backdoors in language models
mls-u3-q08.statement: Why can standard safety training fail to remove a conditional backdoor?

options.a: Safety training reduces the number of tokens the model is able to process
options.b: Training examples rarely contain the trigger, so the behaviour is not exercised
options.c: Conditional behaviour can only be stored in the tokenizer of a model

mls-u3-q08.hint: What has to appear in training in order to correct the behaviour?
mls-u3-q08.explanation: Without the trigger present, the bad branch does not fire during training, so it receives little corrective pressure.
solutionSteps: Without the trigger present, the bad branch does not fire during training, so it receives little corrective pressure.
Choose B: Training examples rarely contain the trigger, so the behaviour is not exercised

mls-u3-q09.title: Provenance and lineage
mls-u3-q09.statement: A vendor’s data feed turns out to have been compromised. What does a record of lineage mainly provide?

options.a: A list of which datasets and models were affected
options.b: A guarantee that the data feed was accurate when it was collected
options.c: An automatic removal of the poisoned samples from the affected data

mls-u3-q09.hint: Lineage records relationships. What can you do with them?
mls-u3-q09.explanation: Lineage scopes the blast radius. It neither certifies the data nor cleans it.
solutionSteps: Lineage scopes the blast radius. It neither certifies the data nor cleans it.
Choose A: A list of which datasets and models were affected

mls-u3-q10.title: Robust statistics
mls-u3-q10.statement: Four participants in federated learning submit values \(0.1\), \(0.2\), \(0.3\) and \(9\) for one coordinate.
mls-u3-q10.hint: With an even count, average the two middle values.
mls-u3-q10.explanation: The two middle values are \(0.2\) and \(0.3\), so the median is \(0.25\). The mean would have been \(2.4\).

mls-u3-q11.title: Detecting poisoned data
mls-u3-q11.statement: A spectral filter finds nothing unusual in a dataset. What is the correct conclusion?

options.a: The dataset has been proven free of every form of poisoning and backdoor
options.b: No detectable signature was found by this method, and poisoning is still possible
options.c: The trained model can now be safely exposed to untrusted users with no limits

mls-u3-q11.hint: How strong is a negative result from a heuristic?
mls-u3-q11.explanation: Heuristic detection can miss attacks designed to avoid it. A negative result is evidence, not proof.
solutionSteps: Heuristic detection can miss attacks designed to avoid it. A negative result is evidence, not proof.
Choose B: No detectable signature was found by this method, and poisoning is still possible

mls-u3-q12.title: Limiting the feedback loop
mls-u3-q12.statement: Which control most directly limits a coordinated group of accounts from shifting a continuously retrained model?

options.a: Capping each account’s influence and delaying promotion of new models
options.b: Raising the learning rate so that the attack finishes sooner than usual
options.c: Publishing the full training data so that all the users can inspect it

mls-u3-q12.hint: Think about the influence of each source and the speed of change.
mls-u3-q12.explanation: Influence caps and held promotion restrict how much and how quickly attacker-controlled data can alter the production model.
solutionSteps: Influence caps and held promotion restrict how much and how quickly attacker-controlled data can alter the production model.

mls-u4-q01.title: Membership inference
mls-u4-q01.statement: Why can learning only that a record was in a training set be a privacy harm?

options.a: Inclusion may itself reveal something sensitive about that person
options.b: It lets the attacker change that record inside the deployed model
options.c: It always reveals every other record contained in the same dataset

mls-u4-q01.hint: Think about a dataset whose members all share a characteristic.
mls-u4-q01.explanation: If the dataset is defined by a sensitive trait, then membership reveals that trait.
solutionSteps: If the dataset is defined by a sensitive trait, then membership reveals that trait.

mls-u4-q02.title: Overfitting as a signal
mls-u4-q02.statement: Which change to a model would most directly weaken a simple loss-threshold membership attack?

options.a: Increasing the size of the model until training loss reaches zero
options.b: Serving predictions from a larger number of replicas of the model
options.c: Reducing the gap between training loss and test loss

mls-u4-q02.explanation: The attack relies on members having lower loss than non-members. Reducing that gap removes the signal it uses.
solutionSteps: The attack relies on members having lower loss than non-members. Reducing that gap removes the signal it uses.
Choose C: Reducing the gap between training loss and test loss

mls-u4-q03.title: Measuring membership risk
mls-u4-q03.statement: A membership attack has a true positive rate of 0.6 and a false positive rate of 0.2.

mls-u4-q04.title: Inversion and attribute inference
mls-u4-q04.statement: An attacker knows a person’s age and postcode, and uses a model’s output to work out their income band. What is this attack called?

options.a: Membership inference
options.b: Backdoor poisoning
options.c: Attribute inference

mls-u4-q04.hint: What is being learned: presence in the data, or a missing field?
mls-u4-q04.explanation: The attacker fills in a hidden attribute of a known person, which is attribute inference.
solutionSteps: The attacker fills in a hidden attribute of a known person, which is attribute inference.
Choose C: Attribute inference

mls-u4-q05.title: Memorisation in language models
mls-u4-q05.statement: Which step most reliably reduces the risk that a model reveals a customer’s secrets from its training data?

options.a: Telling the model in its system prompt never to mention the secrets
options.b: Lowering the temperature used while the model generates responses
options.c: Removing those secrets from the data before training begins

mls-u4-q05.hint: Which option removes the information instead of asking the model not to use it?
mls-u4-q05.explanation: Removing secrets before training reduces direct memorisation of those records. It does not guarantee that sensitive information cannot be inferred or obtained from other data. Prompt instructions and sampling settings do not remove memorised data from the weights.
solutionSteps: Removing secrets before training reduces direct memorisation of those records. It does not guarantee that sensitive information cannot be inferred or obtained from other data. Prompt instructions and sampling settings do not remove memorised data from the weights.
Choose C: Removing those secrets from the data before training begins

mls-u4-q06.title: Canaries
mls-u4-q06.statement: Why are canaries used instead of searching outputs for real customer data?

options.a: They train more quickly than real customer records would normally train
options.b: They are known and harmless, so memorisation can be tested safely
options.c: They stop the model from memorising any other text in the training data

mls-u4-q06.hint: What is special about a string you invented yourself?
mls-u4-q06.explanation: Because the team made up the canary, it knows exactly what to look for, and a leak exposes nothing real.
solutionSteps: Because the team made up the canary, it knows exactly what to look for, and a leak exposes nothing real.

mls-u4-q07.title: Embeddings are personal data too
mls-u4-q07.statement: A team plans to share its vector database with a partner because the raw text has been removed. What is the main concern?

options.b: The vectors become invalid as soon as they leave the original system
options.c: The vectors may still allow much of the original text to be recovered

mls-u4-q07.hint: Is an embedding a one-way, anonymising operation?
mls-u4-q07.explanation: Embeddings preserve a lot of meaning, and inversion attacks can reconstruct text from them, so they stay sensitive.
solutionSteps: Embeddings preserve a lot of meaning, and inversion attacks can reconstruct text from them, so they stay sensitive.
Choose C: The vectors may still allow much of the original text to be recovered

mls-u4-q08.title: Leakage from shared gradients
mls-u4-q08.statement: For a single example in a linear model with a bias, \(\nabla_w\ell = (6, -3)\) and \(\partial\ell/\partial b = 3\).
mls-u4-q08.prompt: What is the first component of the input \(x\)?
mls-u4-q08.hint: Divide the matching component of the weight gradient by the bias gradient.

mls-u4-q09.title: Definition of differential privacy
mls-u4-q09.statement: An algorithm satisfies differential privacy with \(\epsilon = \ln 3\) and \(\delta = 0\).
mls-u4-q09.prompt: At most how many times more likely can any output be when one record is added?
mls-u4-q09.explanation: \(e^{\ln 3} = 3\), so the probability of any output changes by at most a factor of 3.

mls-u4-q10.title: The Laplace mechanism
mls-u4-q10.statement: A query has sensitivity \(\Delta=2\) and the privacy parameter is \(\epsilon=0.5\).
solutionSteps: \(b = \Delta/\epsilon = 2/0.5 = 4\).

mls-u4-q11.title: DP-SGD
mls-u4-q11.statement: A per-example gradient is \(g=(6,8)\) and the clipping norm is \(C=2\).
mls-u4-q11.prompt: What is the first component after clipping?
mls-u4-q11.hint: Find the norm of \(g\), then the scale factor.

mls-u4-q12.title: Privacy budgets
mls-u4-q12.statement: A dashboard answers 25 queries about a dataset, each with \(\epsilon=0.08\).
mls-u4-q12.prompt: Under basic composition, what is the total \(\epsilon\)?
solutionSteps: \(\epsilon_{\text{total}} = 25 \times 0.08 = 2\).

mls-u4-q13.title: Equation-solving extraction

mls-u4-q13.explanation: There are 20 weights and 1 bias, which makes 21 unknowns, so 21 independent equations are required.

mls-u4-q14.title: Surrogate models

mls-u4-q15.title: Limiting extraction

mls-u4-q16.title: Watermarks and fingerprints
mls-u4-q16.statement: A company watermarks its model and concludes that the model can no longer be stolen. What is wrong with this reasoning?

mls-u4-q16.explanation: Watermarks are evidence after the event. Access control and API limits are what make theft harder.
solutionSteps: Watermarks are evidence after the event. Access control and API limits are what make theft harder.

mls-u5-q01.title: Instructions and data share a channel

mls-u5-q02.title: Direct and indirect injection
mls-u5-q02.statement: A user asks an assistant to summarise a web page, and the page contains hidden text directing the assistant to reveal the user’s notes. What is this?

options.b: Direct prompt injection
options.c: Membership inference

mls-u5-q03.title: Injection and jailbreaks

mls-u5-q04.title: System prompts are not secrets

mls-u5-q05.title: The lethal trifecta

mls-u5-q06.title: Exfiltration through rendering

mls-u5-q07.title: Improper output handling
mls-u5-q07.statement: A feature generates SQL with a model and runs it directly using an account that has full database rights. What is the best first fix?

mls-u5-q08.title: Unbounded consumption

mls-u5-q09.title: Retrieved text is untrusted
mls-u5-q09.statement: Why should a company wiki used for retrieval still be treated as partly untrusted?

mls-u5-q10.title: Knowledge poisoning

mls-u5-q11.title: Permissions in retrieval
mls-u5-q11.statement: A multi-tenant RAG service stores all tenants’ documents in one index. Where must tenant isolation be enforced?

mls-u5-q15.title: Constraining output

mls-u5-q16.title: Testing like an attacker

mls-u6-q01.title: Excessive agency

mls-u6-q02.title: The confused deputy

mls-u6-q04.title: Memory as persistence

mls-u6-q05.title: Breaking the trifecta by design

options.b: Frequent prompts lead people to approve without actually reading them

mls-u6-q08.title: Sandboxing and egress control

mls-u7-q04.title: Knowing what you run

mls-u7-q08.title: Monitoring for abuse
